transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the courtyard set design review. We've got two options on the table — a masonry courtyard or a modular painted-timber courtyard — and we need to settle on a construction plan that fits within our $180,000 budget so fabrication can begin. Before I make my final approval decision, I'd like to hear from each of you: structural, permit, stunt, and insurance. Please give me your reports and any concerns you have about either option.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical structural issue. My load test yesterday found that the masonry courtyard design would exceed Soundstage 3's 600 kilograms-per-square-meter floor limit, so that option is not viable from a structural standpoint. The modular painted-timber design does pass, but only if we install a 30-millimeter load-spreading deck. My written report is still in the engineering queue, so I'm sharing these findings verbally now to make sure they're on the record before any approval decision is made.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share a critical heritage-permit finding. I confirmed with the local heritage-permit office this morning that the approved facade may be no wider than exactly 8 meters, and on-stage masonry cutting is prohibited. The permit clerk's email has not yet been added to the production file, so I'm making sure this is on the record now before any approval decision is made. This means the masonry option faces additional permit restrictions beyond the structural issue Jonah raised, and any approved design must stay within the 8-meter facade width limit.

transcript.text: I need to share my rehearsal assessment findings before any approval decision is made. The scripted horse dismount requires an unobstructed lane exactly 10 meters long and 4 meters wide, with a 2-meter crash mat at its landing end. This lane requirement must be accommodated in whichever courtyard design we approve. The choreography note is still awaiting the next stunt meeting, so I'm putting this on the record now.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to share a critical insurance finding before any approval decision is made. I confirmed with the insurer's underwriter that our coverage excludes an open-flame brazier on this stage. However, an LED-flame prop is permitted under the policy if it remains at least 12 meters from the sprinkler-head cluster and its certification is filed before filming. The endorsement is currently awaiting countersignature, so I'm putting this on the record now to make sure the approved design accounts for these insurance constraints.
